title: Effect semantic compatibility
summary: Normative semantic adapter boundary between ResultSafe Cause and Exit concepts and Effect concepts.

scope: Compatibility describes adapter meanings only and does not assert shared code, runtime types, constructors, wire formats, branding, equality, hashing, or release compatibility
Adapters are explicit opt-in integration code and MUST NOT alter Result<T,E> or introduce an Effect runtime dependency into the core model

cause_mappings.requirement: Map absence of cause without synthesizing a failure.
Preserve E through the explicitly supplied E adapter or codec.
Convert between an Effect defect and portable Failure explicitly; runtime defect identity is not portable.
Convert interruption context to portable Failure explicitly; runtime fiber identity is not portable.
Preserve binary grouping and left-to-right order.
Preserve binary grouping and deterministic child order without claiming temporal ordering.

exit_mappings.requirement: Preserve T through the explicitly supplied T adapter or codec.
Apply the Cause mapping recursively; Empty remains a valid ResultSafe failure cause even if a target adapter cannot represent it.

loss_policy: An adapter MUST report or reject semantic loss and MUST NOT silently flatten, reorder, deduplicate, re-associate, or discard Cause nodes
If the target version cannot represent Exit.Failure(Empty), conversion MUST fail explicitly rather than inventing a defect or success
Failure.causes MUST NOT be consulted as a substitute for Effect or ResultSafe Cause topology

qualification.claim_scope: The separate adapter is locally qualified only for exact effect@3.22.1; this is not release approval, promotion, or publication evidence.
